doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Chicago clarinetists and trumpeters from New Orleans
summary: Williams and Hinton recall the New Orleans players in Chicago, including Jimmy Noone, the Dodds brothers, Scoops Carey and trumpeter Bob Shaffner.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Oh, when I went to Englewood High School, it was predominantly white. I mean it was over 80/20 white when I went there in 1933, back in 33, 34, 35 and 36, and 37, the end of that four year period. But the music though, in our town, was the thing that really astounded me.
What was the name of those brothers, one played clarinet, the other played from, they came from New Orleans?

Olhan Brothers, yes, but they had a bunch of people that came from New Orleans there that was really doing it. Jimmy Noone and the bunch. They could do it in the box, you know, and the guys that played clarinet. A lot of clarinet players came up.
Oh, yeah, every gig, [inaudible] they had Scoops Carey.
Bob — oh God what was his name, the trumpet player? Real black cat, man, Bob something, he was a lead trumpet player, a beautiful trumpet. Bob something.
